newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up in broad trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up in broad trade.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher in active trade on Friday, as investors bought shares of corporates which were expected to post good profits in 1997, brokers said.
The all share index closed 5.5 points up at 739.3. price gains outnumbered declines by 47 to 18. Hayleys rose 10 rupees to 245, Lanka Lubricants 1.25 to 53.
"Since buyers have begun to show they are willing to pay premiums, the all share is moving up," said Dihan Dedigama of John Keells Stock Brokers.
Buyers have been forced to pay premiums since corporate profits for the year to March have been exceptionally good, and forecasts for the year to December are even better, brokers said.
Turnover was 61.21 million rupees, led by 30,000 Brewery, 45,000 Hayleys and 710,500 United Motors.
Brokers said the stock exchange, which began screen-based trading trials this week, saw improvements in trading due to easing of bottlenecks which existed under the old open outcry system.
A significant amount of an average 20 percent of daily transactions which did not get executed under the old open outcry system are now getting done, they said.
Officials expect to fully implement screen-based trading in six weeks' time, after all 15 brokers are connected to the exchange through radio links. -- Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
